questions.q: Match each primary derivative of the mesoderm with what it gives rise to — 1) Paraxial mesoderm 2) Lateral plate mesoderm 3) Intermediate mesoderm … A) Somatopleure and splanchnopleuric layers B) Somites, muscles and myotomes C) Urogenital system (together with endoderm)
questions.exp: Paraxial mesoderm forms the somites, muscles and myotomes; the lateral plate mesoderm splits into somatopleure and splanchnopleure; the intermediate mesoderm (with endoderm) builds the urogenital system and cloaca. (Book p705)

questions.q: Fill up: The somatopleure of the lateral plate mesoderm contributes to the outer parietal pleura, the outer peritoneum, and ______.
questions.exp: Somatopleure forms the outer (parietal) serosal layers — parietal pleura, peritoneum and pericardium — while splanchnopleure forms the inner (visceral) layers. (Book p705)

questions.q: All of the following are derivatives of the splanchnopleure EXCEPT:
questions.exp: The outer parietal pleura is a somatopleuric derivative; the splanchnopleure gives the inner visceral pleura, inner peritoneum and inner pericardium. (Book p705)

questions.q: According to the notes, the urogenital system develops from the intermediate mesoderm together with which other germ layer?
questions.exp: The notes state the development of the urogenital system as intermediate mesoderm + endoderm, which together form the cloaca. (Book p705)

questions.q: The cloaca is best defined as the:
opts: Midgut segment between the yolk sac and the allantois
Foregut cranial to the tracheoesophageal septum
Urogenital sinus distal to the bladder
questions.exp: Cloaca = hindgut distal to the allantois; it then divides into the primitive urogenital sinus and the primitive rectum. (Book p705)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the anorectal embryology is TRUE?
opts: The anal canal below the pectinate line is derived from the proctoderm (anal pit)
The anal canal above the pectinate line is derived from the proctoderm
The entire anal canal is derived from endoderm of the primitive rectum
The pectinate line separates two endodermal segments of the cloaca
questions.exp: The anal canal below the pectinate line is derived from the proctoderm (anal pit); the part up to the pectinate line comes from the primitive rectum (cloacal endoderm). (Book p705)

questions.q: During anorectal surgery a trainee points out the pectinate line and asks for the embryological origin of the canal below it. According to the notes, the correct reply is:
opts: Intermediate mesoderm of the nephrogenic cord
questions.exp: Below the pectinate line the anal canal is proctodermal (anal pit); the canal up to the pectinate line derives from the cloaca (primitive rectum). (Book p705)

questions.q: The cloaca divides into the primitive rectum and the:
questions.exp: The cloaca splits into the primitive urogenital sinus and the primitive rectum; only the urogenital sinus further subdivides into epithelial buds, vesicourethral canal and definitive urogenital sinus. (Book p705)

questions.q: Match each derivative of the primitive urogenital sinus with its fate — 1) Epithelial buds 2) Vesicourethral canal 3) Definitive urogenital sinus … A) Bladder and part of the urethra B) Prostate C) Pelvic and phallic parts of the urethra
questions.exp: Epithelial buds give the prostate; the vesicourethral canal gives the bladder and part of the urethra; the definitive urogenital sinus gives the pelvic and phallic urethral parts. (Book p705)

questions.q: Fill up: In males, the vesicourethral canal forms the prostatic urethra up to the opening of the ______.
questions.exp: In males the vesicourethral canal forms the prostatic urethra up to the opening of the ejaculatory duct; in females it forms part of the urethra. (Book p705)

questions.q: In males, the pelvic part of the definitive urogenital sinus forms:
opts: The remaining prostatic urethra and the membranous urethra
The bladder and the whole urethra
questions.exp: Pelvic part → urethra: in males the remaining prostatic urethra and the membranous urethra; in females a part of the urethra. (Book p705)

questions.q: All of the following are derivatives of the pelvic part of the definitive urogenital sinus EXCEPT:
questions.exp: The pelvic part forms the remaining prostatic urethra and membranous urethra in males, and part of the urethra in females; the spongy urethra is a phallic-part derivative. (Book p705)

questions.q: The primitive rectum gives rise to the rectum and to which segment of the anal canal?
opts: The anal canal up to the pectinate line
The anal canal distal to the pectinate line
Neither — the anal canal is wholly proctodermal
questions.exp: Primitive rectum → rectum with the anal canal up to the pectinate line; the canal below the pectinate line is proctodermal. (Book p705)

questions.q: Fill up: In females, the vesicourethral canal contributes to the ______.
questions.exp: The vesicourethral canal forms the bladder and, in females, part of the urethra (in males, the prostatic urethra up to the ejaculatory duct opening). (Book p705)

questions.q: Match each intermediate-mesoderm structure with its fate — 1) Mesonephric (Wolffian) duct 2) Paramesonephric (Müllerian) duct 3) Urogenital ridge … A) Gives the ureteric bud, which forms the collecting system of the kidney B) Remnants include the appendix of the testis and the hydatid of Morgagni C) Has a medial genital ridge and a lateral nephrogenic cord
questions.exp: Wolffian duct → ureteric bud → collecting system; Müllerian duct → appendix of testis and hydatid of Morgagni remnants; the urogenital ridge carries the medial genital ridge and lateral nephrogenic cord. (Book p706)

questions.q: Fill up: The ureteric bud, which arises from the mesonephric duct, forms the ______ of the kidneys.
questions.exp: Mesonephric (Wolffian) duct → ureteric bud → collecting system of the kidneys; the nephrogenic cord (metanephric mesenchyme) forms the excretory part. (Book p706)

questions.q: The urogenital ridge extends over which regions of the embryo?
questions.exp: The urogenital ridge extends from the cervical to the sacral region, adjacent to the Wolffian duct, as paired swellings on either side of the dorsal aorta. (Book p706)

questions.q: In the urogenital ridge, the lateral swelling (nephrogenic cord) forms the:
questions.exp: The medial swelling (genital ridge) forms the ovary and testis; the lateral swelling (nephrogenic cord) forms the excretory part of the kidney. (Book p706)

questions.q: All of the following are true of the urogenital ridge EXCEPT:
opts: Its medial swelling forms the nephrogenic cord
It lies adjacent to the Wolffian duct
It appears as paired swellings on either side of the dorsal aorta
It extends from the cervical to the sacral region
questions.exp: The medial swelling is the genital ridge (→ ovary, testis); the lateral swelling is the nephrogenic cord (→ excretory part of the kidney). (Book p706)

questions.q: Match each embryological remnant with its ductal origin — 1) Appendix of the epididymis 2) Appendix of the testis 3) Hydatid of Morgagni … A) Paramesonephric (Müllerian) duct B) Mesonephric (Wolffian) duct C) Ureteric bud
questions.exp: Appendix of the epididymis is a remnant of the mesonephric duct; the appendix of the testis and the hydatid of Morgagni are remnants of the paramesonephric duct. (Book p706)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the metanephros is TRUE?
opts: The metanephros regresses within a few days
The metanephros forms only the collecting system
The metanephros is the functional kidney of adult amphibians in humans
questions.exp: Metanephros = the (permanent) kidney. The pronephros regresses in a few days; the mesonephros (kidney of amphibians and reptiles) regresses by 4 months and has no role in humans. (Book p706)

questions.q: According to the development timeline, the pronephros forms on which day of embryonic life?
questions.exp: Formation of the pronephros occurs on day 22 (4th week); it regresses in a few days. (Book p706)

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the pronephros?
opts: It regresses within a few days of formation
It persists as the adult kidney
It functions as the definitive human kidney in utero
questions.exp: The pronephros forms on day 22 (4th week) and regresses in a few days; the metanephros is the permanent kidney. (Book p706)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the mesonephros is TRUE?
opts: It forms the permanent human kidney
It functions as the kidney in adult humans
It is the working kidney of amphibians and reptiles in humans
questions.exp: The mesonephros forms by the end of the 4th week, regresses by 4 months and has no role in humans (it is the kidney of amphibians and reptiles). (Book p706)

questions.q: In the 5th week of development, which of the following occurs?
opts: Metanephric blastema from the nephrogenic cord; ureteric bud epithelium from the mesonephric duct
First fully formed nephron appears and nephrogenesis is completed by the end of the week
Urine formation (filtration) begins and the kidney ascends to the lumbar region with rotation
Pronephros forms from the nephrogenic cord and regresses completely within a few days
questions.exp: 5th week: mesenchyme of the metanephric blastema forms from the nephrogenic cord and epithelium of the ureteric bud from the mesonephric duct. First fully formed nephron = end of 8th week; filtration begins 9–10 wk with ascent and rotation; pronephros forms on day 22 and regresses within days. (Book p706)

questions.q: The epithelial-mesenchymal interaction (transition) that drives nephron formation occurs between the ureteric bud epithelium and the:
questions.exp: In weeks 6–8 the epithelial-mesenchymal interaction/transition occurs between the epithelium of the ureteric bud and the mesenchyme of the metanephric bud, under WT1 control. (Book p707)

questions.q: Fill up: WT1, required for the epithelial-mesenchymal interaction, is a ______ located on chromosome ______.
questions.exp: WT1 is a transcription factor on chromosome 11, acting in the 6–8th week epithelial-mesenchymal interaction between ureteric bud epithelium and metanephric mesenchyme. (Book p707)

questions.q: The first fully formed nephron appears by when in the timeline?
questions.exp: End of the 8th week = first fully formed nephron. (Book p707)

questions.q: During the 9th–10th weeks of fetal life, which pair of events occurs?
opts: Urine formation (filtration) begins and the kidney ascends with rotation
The pronephros regresses and the mesonephros forms
questions.exp: 9–10 weeks: formation of urine (filtration) and ascent of the kidney with rotation. (Book p707)

questions.q: Nephrogenesis is completed at which gestational age?
questions.exp: Nephrogenesis completes at 32–36 weeks, with 60–70% of nephrons forming in the 3rd trimester. (Book p707)

questions.q: Fill up: 60–70% of all nephrons are formed during the ______.
questions.exp: 60–70% of nephrons are formed in the 3rd trimester; nephrogenesis completes at 32–36 weeks. (Book p707)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about nephrons from birth onward is TRUE?
opts: No new nephron is formed or replaced after birth
Nephrons are continuously replaced by division
The nephron number keeps increasing until age 5
questions.exp: At birth the number of nephrons is fixed; no new nephron is formed or replaced after birth. (Book p707)

questions.q: Urine concentration capacity reaches adult level by which age?
questions.exp: After birth, urine concentration capacity increases and reaches the adult level by 1.5 years. (Book p707)

questions.q: Fill up: The defining parameter of the nephron number is the ______.
questions.exp: Nephron number defining parameter: birth weight — the starting point of the CKD pathogenesis flowchart. (Book p707)

questions.q: An adult born at low birth weight is found to have a reduced number of functional nephrons. According to the notes' pathogenesis chain, what is the earliest haemodynamic consequence?
opts: Rise in single-nephron GFR with glomerular hyperfiltration
questions.exp: ↓ Birth weight → ↓ no. of functional nephrons → ↑ single-nephron GFR (GFR = single-nephron GFR × no. of functional nephrons) → glomerular hyperfiltration → intraglomerular hypertension → hyperfiltration injury. (Book p707)

questions.q: Match each step of the hyperfiltration-injury cascade with the step that immediately follows it — 1) Intraglomerular hypertension 2) Stretching of the capillary pore 3) Proteinuria (albuminuria) … A) Hyperfiltration injury B) Increased diameter of the capillary pore C) Tubular injury
questions.exp: The cascade runs: intraglomerular hypertension → hyperfiltration injury → stretching of the capillary pore → ↑ diameter of the capillary pore → proteinuria (albuminuria) → tubular injury. (Book p707)

questions.q: In the CKD pathogenesis flowchart, proteinuria (albuminuria) leads to:
opts: Dilatation of capillary pores with normalisation of GFR
questions.exp: Proteinuria (albuminuria) → tubular injury → interstitial inflammation → TGF-β release → fibrosis of tubules and interstitium → CKD. (Book p707)

questions.q: Fill up: Interstitial inflammation triggers release of ______, which drives fibrosis of the tubules and interstitium.
questions.exp: TGF-β release from interstitial inflammation produces fibrosis of the tubules and interstitium, culminating in CKD. (Book p707)

questions.q: As written in the notes, total GFR equals single-nephron GFR multiplied by the:
questions.exp: GFR = single-nephron GFR × no. of functional nephrons — which is why fewer nephrons force each remaining nephron to hyperfilter. (Book p707)

questions.q: According to the notes, CKD features a reduction in the number of functional nephrons together with:
opts: Interstitial fibrosis, tubular atrophy and glomerulosclerosis
Cystic dilatation of all collecting ducts
questions.exp: CKD features: ↓ in no. of functional nephrons with a percentage of interstitial fibrosis, tubular atrophy and glomerulo-sclerosis. (Book p708)

questions.q: A woman with pre-eclampsia delivers a small-for-gestational-age baby. According to the notes' maternal-factor cascade, this child is at increased risk of all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Pre-eclampsia/hypertension → placental insufficiency → IUGR → SGA baby → ↑ risk of CKD, hypertension, hyperuricaemia, diabetes and metabolic syndrome. (Book p708)

questions.q: Match each step of the maternal-factor cascade with the step that follows it — 1) Age of conception 2) Placental insufficiency 3) Intra-uterine growth retardation … A) Placental insufficiency B) Small-for-gestational-age (SGA) baby C) Pre-eclampsia / hypertension
questions.exp: Age of conception → pre-eclampsia/hypertension → placental insufficiency → intra-uterine growth retardation → SGA baby → ↑ risk of CKD, hypertension, hyperuricaemia, diabetes, metabolic syndrome. (Book p708)

questions.q: Which gene is described in the notes as important for the formation of the epithelium of the ureteric bud?
questions.exp: PAX-2 is important for formation of the epithelium of the ureteric bud; WT1 drives the epithelial-mesenchymal interaction instead. (Book p708)

questions.q: Match each vertebral level with its structure — 1) Adult kidney 2) Fetal kidney 3) Hilum … A) S1–S5 B) T12–L3 C) L1
questions.exp: Location of kidney: fetal S1–S5, ascending with rotation to the adult T12–L3; the hilum lies at L1. (Book p708)

questions.q: The WAGR syndrome of WT1 mutation comprises Wilms tumour, aniridia and genitourinary abnormalities, plus:
questions.exp: WAGR = Wilms tumour, Aniridia, Genitourinary abnormalities, Retardation (mental). Hypoglycaemia, omphalocele and macroglossia belong to Beckwith-Wiedemann (WT2). (Book p708)

questions.q: All of the following are components of the WAGR syndrome EXCEPT:
questions.exp: WAGR = Wilms tumour, aniridia, genitourinary abnormalities and mental retardation; macroglossia is a Beckwith-Wiedemann feature. (Book p708)

questions.q: Denys-Drash syndrome (WT1) comprises Wilms tumour and disorders of sexual development, together with:
opts: Diffuse mesangial sclerosis with early-onset CKD by 3–5 years
Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis with renal failure by 15–20 years
Nephronophthisis with renal failure by 20 years
Minimal change disease with steroid-dependent relapses
questions.exp: Denys-Drash: Wilms tumour, DSD (male pseudohermaphroditism), diffuse mesangial sclerosis → early-onset CKD by 3–5 years. (Book p709)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about Denys-Drash syndrome is TRUE?
opts: The associated disorder of sexual development is male pseudohermaphroditism
The renal lesion is focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
It results from a WT2 gene mutation
questions.exp: Denys-Drash (WT1): Wilms tumour, male pseudohermaphroditism and diffuse mesangial sclerosis with CKD by 3–5 years; FSGS with renal failure by 15–20 years is Frasier syndrome. (Book p709)

questions.q: In Frasier syndrome, the gonadal involvement includes gonadoblastoma and gonadal dysgenesis with:
questions.exp: Frasier syndrome: gonadoblastoma, gonadal dysgenesis with normal external genitalia; biopsy shows focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, with renal failure by 15–20 years. (Book p709)

questions.q: Match each syndrome with its characteristic renal lesion and course — 1) Denys-Drash syndrome 2) Frasier syndrome 3) Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome … A) Diffuse mesangial sclerosis → CKD by 3–5 years B) Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis → renal failure by 15–20 years C) Genomic imprinting anomaly with organomegaly
questions.exp: Denys-Drash → diffuse mesangial sclerosis (CKD by 3–5 years); Frasier → FSGS (renal failure by 15–20 years); Beckwith-Wiedemann → imprinting anomaly with macroglossia, umbilical hernia and organomegaly. (Book p709)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the WT2 gene is TRUE?
opts: It has no role in the epithelial-mesenchymal interaction
It is the transcription factor on chromosome 11
Its mutation produces the WAGR syndrome
It forms the epithelium of the ureteric bud
questions.exp: WT2 has no role in the epithelial-mesenchymal interaction (that is WT1's role); WT2-associated syndromes are Beckwith-Wiedemann and Russell Silver. (Book p709)

questions.q: Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome is caused by a:
questions.exp: Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome = genomic imprinting anomaly (WT2). (Book p709)

questions.q: All of the following are features of Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Triangular facies (with mental retardation) belongs to Russell Silver syndrome; BWS has macroglossia, umbilical hernia, omphalocele, haemihypertrophy, Wilms tumour, microcephaly/ear lobe crease, hypoglycaemia and organomegaly. (Book p709)

questions.q: Fill up: In Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, organomegaly includes nephromegaly, hepatosplenomegaly and ______.
questions.exp: The organomegaly of BWS is nephromegaly, hepatosplenomegaly and adrenomegaly (shown in the notes' ultrasound images). (Book p709)

questions.q: Which of the following is listed under 'Others' for Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome?
questions.exp: Others in BWS: haemihypertrophy of limbs, omphalocele, Wilms tumour, microcephaly/ear lobe crease, hypoglycaemia and medullary sponge kidney (in adults). (Book p709)

questions.q: Fill up: The adult renal association listed with Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome is ______.
questions.exp: Medullary sponge kidney (in adults) is the adult renal association listed with BWS. (Book p709)

questions.q: The two photographs on the Beckwith-Wiedemann page of the notes show macroglossia and an:
questions.exp: The BWS figures show macroglossia and umbilical hernia, with a separate ultrasound panel of organomegaly (nephromegaly, hepatosplenomegaly, adrenomegaly). (Book p709)

questions.q: Russell Silver syndrome is characterised by:
questions.exp: Russell Silver syndrome (WT2): triangular facies and mental retardation. (Book p709)

questions.q: The incidence of unilateral renal agenesis is:
questions.exp: Unilateral renal agenesis occurs in 1 in 10,000 live births, more often in females, with a PAX-2 mutation. (Book p710)

questions.q: Unilateral renal agenesis is more common in which sex, and is associated with which mutation?
questions.exp: F > M; PAX-2 mutation. (Book p710)

questions.q: All of the following are listed associations of unilateral renal agenesis EXCEPT:
opts: Hypertension due to reduced nephron number
questions.exp: Associations: optic nerve coloboma, dextrocardia, hypertension (due to ↓ nephron number) and flat foot; aniridia belongs to WAGR (WT1). (Book p710)

questions.q: Which of the following is a listed association of unilateral renal agenesis?
questions.exp: Associations include flat foot, optic nerve coloboma, dextrocardia and hypertension from reduced nephron number. (Book p710)

questions.q: An abdominal radiograph and ultrasound are requested for a child suspected of unilateral renal agenesis. The expected findings illustrated in the notes are:
opts: An empty renal fossa with a single functioning kidney
A horseshoe fusion of both kidneys
questions.exp: The notes' images (CXR, IVP, USG) of unilateral renal agenesis show the absent kidney with a single functioning kidney in the opposite fossa. (Book p710)

questions.q: Bilateral renal agenesis is known as Potter's syndrome and is associated with a mutation of:
questions.exp: Bilateral renal agenesis = Potter's syndrome; the book associates it with a RET gene/GDNF protein (glial derived neurotrophic factor) mutation, unlike unilateral agenesis which is linked to PAX-2. (Book p710)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about Potter's syndrome is TRUE?
opts: It is the most common cause of death immediately after birth
It results from a PAX-2 mutation
It results from a WT1 gene mutation
It is commonly associated with aniridia
questions.exp: Potter's syndrome (bilateral renal agenesis) is the m/c cause of death immediately after birth, with a RET gene/GDNF protein mutation. (Book p710)

questions.q: All of the following are illustrated in the notes' figure of Potter's syndrome EXCEPT:
questions.exp: The figure shows pulmonary hyperplasia (as labelled in the notes), absent kidneys with absent renal arteries, and a disc-shaped adrenal gland; macroglossia is a Beckwith-Wiedemann feature. (Book p710)

units.title: Mesoderm derivatives & urogenital system
units.guide: Mesoderm splits into paraxial, intermediate and lateral plate derivatives. The lateral plate divides into somatopleure (outer serosal layers) and splanchnopleure (inner serosal layers). The urogenital system is built from intermediate mesoderm plus endoderm, which together form the cloaca.

units.title: Cloaca & urogenital sinus differentiation
units.guide: The cloaca — the hindgut distal to the allantois — divides into the primitive urogenital sinus and the primitive rectum. The sinus's epithelial buds, vesicourethral canal and definitive urogenital sinus form the prostate, bladder and urethral segments, while the rectum carries the anal canal only up to the pectinate line, below which the canal is proctodermal.

units.title: Intermediate mesoderm: ducts & urogenital ridge
units.guide: The intermediate mesoderm gives the Wolffian and Müllerian ducts and the urogenital ridge. The Wolffian duct throws off the ureteric bud that becomes the collecting system, while the ridge's medial genital ridge forms the gonads and its lateral nephrogenic cord forms the excretory part of the kidney. The metanephros is the permanent kidney.

units.title: Timeline of kidney development
units.guide: The pronephros appears on day 22 and vanishes within days, the mesonephros by 4 months, and the metanephros is the permanent kidney. The first fully formed nephron appears by the end of week 8; nephrogenesis completes at 32–36 weeks with the nephron number fixed at birth, and urine concentration reaches adult level by 1.5 years.

units.title: CKD pathogenesis: nephron endowment
units.guide: Birth weight defines the nephron number. Fewer functional nephrons force each nephron to hyperfilter — intraglomerular hypertension, capillary-pore stretching, albuminuria, tubular injury and TGF-β-driven fibrosis — ending in CKD with interstitial fibrosis, tubular atrophy and glomerulosclerosis.

units.title: Maternal factors, PAX-2 & kidney location
units.guide: Maternal pre-eclampsia/hypertension produces placental insufficiency, IUGR and SGA offspring at risk of CKD, hypertension, hyperuricaemia, diabetes and metabolic syndrome. PAX-2 builds the ureteric bud epithelium, and the fetal kidney at S1–S5 ascends with rotation to the adult T12–L3, hilum at L1.

units.title: WT1 syndromes: WAGR, Denys-Drash & Frasier
units.guide: WT1 mutations produce three syndromes. WAGR = Wilms tumour, aniridia, genitourinary abnormalities and mental retardation. Denys-Drash gives diffuse mesangial sclerosis with CKD by 3–5 years, while Frasier gives FSGS with renal failure by 15–20 years and normal external genitalia.

units.title: WT2 syndromes: Beckwith-Wiedemann & Russell Silver
units.guide: WT2 has no role in the epithelial-mesenchymal interaction. Its imprinting-related mutations cause Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome — macroglossia, umbilical hernia, organomegaly, Wilms tumour and hypoglycaemia — and Russell Silver syndrome with triangular facies and mental retardation.

units.title: Renal agenesis: unilateral & Potter's syndrome
units.guide: Unilateral renal agenesis (1 in 10,000, F > M, PAX-2 mutation) associates with optic nerve coloboma, dextrocardia, hypertension and flat foot. Bilateral agenesis (Potter's syndrome) is the most common cause of death immediately after birth and is linked to the RET gene/GDNF protein.
